COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law and the state finance law, in relation to the creation of the cigarette tax enforcement fund; and making an appropriation therefor
items.lawCode: Amd §§472, 482, 1846, 483 & 1814, Tax L; add §97-qqqq, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5701

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the tax law and the state finance law,
in relation to the creation of the cigarette tax enforcement fund; and
making an appropriation therefor

PURPOSE:  To increase enforcement of the Cigarette Tax and quell the
influx of illegal cigarettes in New York markets.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS: Section one of this bill amends Section 472(1)
of the Tax Law to allow the Commissioner of the Department of Taxation
and Finance (the "Commissioner") to prescribe, prepare and furnish
stamps for the payment by the agent of the four cents per stamp
concurrent expense allowance that is required to be deposited in the
Cigarette Tax Enforcement Fund (the "Fund"), which is established in
section three of this bill.

Section two of this bill adds a new subdivision (c) to Tax Law section
482. This new subdivision requires the Commissioner to deposit all
taxes, fees, interest and penalties collected or received from the
amount received pursuant to Tax Law section 482(1) into the Fund.

Section three of this bill amends the State Finance Law by adding a
new section 97-qqqq to establish the Cigarette Tax Enforcement Fund.
The Fund is in joint custody of the State Comptroller and the
Commissioner. The Comptroller is authorized and directed to receive
for deposit to the credit of the Fund monies received from the
Commissioner from the concurrent expense allowance, sale of forfeited
cigarettes, and other monies appropriated, credited or transferred
thereto from any other fund or source and the Cigarette Marketing
Standards Act. Monies in the Fund will be distributed to the Division
of the State Police for cigarette tax enforcement purposes and used to
pay those people who qualify for a reward under the rewards program
established pursuant to section six of this bill.

Section four of this bill amends subdivisions (a), (b) and (c) of Tax
Law section 1846 to provide the procedure for the sale, redemption and
disposal of cigarettes that have been forfeited to the State due to
violations of Criminal Procedure Law sections 1.20 or 2.10. All
cigarettes that have been determined to be counterfeit or violate
import laws must be destroyed. All revenue received is required to be
deposited into the Fund.

Section five of this bill amends subparagraph (B) of Section 483(b)(1)
of the Tax Law, relating to the "cost of the agent," to provide that,
in the absence of the filing with the commissioner of satisfactory
proof of a lesser cost of doing business of the agent making the sale,
the cost of doing business by the agent shall be presumed to be 2.25%
of the basic cost of cigarettes for sales to wholesale dealers plus 1
cent per package of 10 cigarettes, 2 cents per package of 20
cigarettes and 2.5 cents for each 5 cigarettes in excess of 20
cigarettes for packages in excess of 20 cigarettes. The cost of doing
business by the agent shall be presumed to be 5.75% of the basic cost
of cigarettes for sales to chain stores plus 1 cent per package of 10
cigarettes, 2 cents per package of 20 cigarettes and 2.5 cents for
each 5 cigarettes in excess of 20 cigarettes for packages in excess of
20 cigarettes. The cost of doing business by the agent shall be


presumed to be 5.75% of the basic cost of cigarettes with respect to
sales to retail dealers plus 1 cent per package of 10 cigarettes, 2
cents per package of 20 cigarettes and 2.5 cents for each 5 cigarettes
in excess of 20 cigarettes for packages in excess of 20 cigarettes.

This section of the bill also amends subparagraph (B) of Section
483(b)(2) of the Tax Law, relating to the "cost of the wholesale
dealer," to provide that, in the absence of the filing with the
commissioner of satisfactory proof of a lesser cost of doing business
of the wholesale dealer making the sale, the cost of doing business by
the wholesale dealer shall be presumed to be 1% of the basic cost of
cigarettes, and with respect to sales to chain stores, 3.5% of the
basic cost of cigarettes.

This section of the bill lastly amends subparagraph (B) of Section
483(b)(3) of the Tax Law, relating to the "cost of the retail dealer,"
to provide that, in the absence of the filing with the commissioner of
satisfactory proof of a lesser cost of doing business of the retail
dealer making the sale, the cost of doing business by the retail
dealer shall be presumed to be 8.5% of the sum of the basic cost of
cigarettes plus the cost of doing business by the agent with respect
to cigarettes sold to retail dealers

Section six of this bill amends Tax Law section 1814 by adding a new
subdivision (j) to provide that the Commissioner shall establish a
program to allow individuals to submit a sworn statement affirming the
observation of a violation of the Cigarette Tax and, where the
Commissioner deems it appropriate, allow for a reward for any such
sworn statement. Where enforcement action is taken pursuant to Tax Law
article 37 or article 20 based upon a sworn statement, the
Commissioner shall offer as a reward to such individual or individuals
that provided a sworn statement an amount that, in the aggregate, is
five dollars. No peace officer, police officer or employee of the
department, employee of any company under contract with the
department, or employee of any governmental entity that, in
conjunction with the department, conducts enforcement activity
relating to a violation of Article 37 or Article 20 of this chapter,
shall be entitled to obtain the benefit of any such reward when acting
in the discharge of his or her official duties. All rewards paid
pursuant to this section shall be paid from the Cigarette Tax
Enforcement Fund.

Section seven of this bill appropriates to the Division of the State
Police $6,000,000 from the Cigarette Tax Enforcement Fund to support
cigarette tax enforcement activities and prescribes other methods in
which the appropriation may be used in efforts to enforce the
cigarette tax.

Section eight of this bill provides that this act shall take effect on
the first day of the sales tax quarterly period, as described in
subdivision (b) of section 1136 of the tax law, next succeeding the
thirtieth day after it shall have become a law and shall apply in
accordance with the applicable transitional provisions of section 1106
and 1217 of the tax law.

JUSTIFICATION:  The "presumed cost of doing business" for cigarette
stamping agents, which was enacted to help defer the cost of acting as


the State's agent for .the collection of the cigarette excise tax, has
not increased since 1999. Since 1999, the cigarette excise tax has
increased almost three hundred percent, which stamping agents are
required to prepay. This prepayment burden, in addition to a variety
of other factors, has caused the cost of doing business for cigarette
stamping agents to well exceed the "presumed cost of doing business"
provided by the Tax Law. To bring the "presumed cost of doing
business" more in line with the actual cost of doing business, the
"presumed cost of doing business" requires an adjustment. This bill
makes such an adjustment, which will enable the stamping agents to
remain in business and help secure tax collection.

Because of the significant influx of cigarettes that are either
unstamped or bear a stamp from another State into New York markets,
this bill provides a revenue stream for the enforcement of the State's
laws regarding the sale and taxation of cigarettes. With this revenue
stream, the State's enforcement efforts should increase and the number
of unstamped and stamped with another State's stamp cigarettes being
sold in New York should decrease. This will increase the revenues to
the State because more stamps will be sold.  Additionally, when
cigarettes are forfeited through the increased enforcement activities,
their sale will generate revenue to the State.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  Similar to:  2014: S.1958-D -Referred to
Investigations and Government Operations 2013: S.1958-C - Passed the
Senate 2011-2: S.4763-A - Passed the Senate both years

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  By increasing the minimum price of cigarettes
sold in New York, the State will collect increased sales tax revenues.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect on the first day of the
sales tax quarterly period, as described in subdivision (b) of section
1136 of the tax law, next succeeding the thirtieth day after it shall
have become a law and shall apply in accordance with the applicable
transitional provisions of section 1106 and 1217 of the tax law.
